title: Is the map asking for something that does not exist?
description: A map cell names an artifact; the artifact must resolve to a scene on disk. When a pipeline stage regresses with no commit to blame, or a sequence's artifact stage reads 9x% for no visible reason, this is the first thing to check -- and it is invisible to the pathfinder, to git status and to git log -S.
triggers: pipeline global_avg dropped and no commit explains it
a sequence's stage 3 reads 97-99% instead of OK
a map places an artifact that does not appear in game
after any tool writes generated content back into a hand-authored map

steps.why: spine scope, the same denominator the pipeline scorer uses. Exit code = unresolved placements.
whole corpus. Read the note line about non-standard empty cells -- the scorer counts those as placements even though this gate does not.
absent = renamed or superseded; present without a scene = a delegate_to chain that does not terminate.
names the commit that introduced it. If empty, the cell is uncommitted -- a class both concurrency instruments miss.

steps.do: grep the token in commons/data/museum/em_plan.json and the generators
steps.why: a spine map that is also a museum hall has TWO authors. floor_anchor entered Point_Lines this way; the plan is derived FROM the map, so fixing the map is sufficient.

steps.do: read the registry description of the nearest surviving name
steps.why: supersession is usually stated in prose. calder_mobile's description names calder_mobile_primaries as the thing it replaced.

steps.do: Edit the cell (never Set-Content -- PS 5.1 writes a BOM), then re-run steps 1 and the pipeline scorer
steps.why: the delta is the proof. Do not carry a remembered global_avg; take it.

gotchas: A gate that scanned zero maps prints identically to a clean corpus. Check the denominator in the header line before believing OK.
GridInteractablesComponent dispatches mc:, gridagent:, criticalinfo: and cluster: BEFORE the registry. They are not lookup names and must not be demanded to resolve as such.
Removing a dead cell is behaviour-preserving (it rendered nothing). Substituting a live artifact is a content decision that belongs to the map's author.
